slides: Let's continue with circles, with one more arc and a few more words.

slides.say: Here's one more arc, a bigger one, from P to Q, along the bottom. The central angle at O intercepts it. And an inscribed angle from D, up at the top, intercepts it too. Stand at D and look down between the two chords. What you see is the arc P Q. So the arc an angle intercepts is always the one between its arms, on the side it opens to.
at: And an inscribed angle from D

slides.say: A few more words that come up a lot. A tangent is a straight line that touches the circle at exactly one point. Here's a tangent. It touches the circle at T, and it doesn't go inside.
at: A tangent is a straight line

slides.say: We can draw a tangent at any point of the circle. Here's one, and here's another. Each one touches the circle at just one point.
A line that goes through the circle, and crosses it at two points, is not a tangent. And a line that misses the circle isn't one either. The rules of tangents get their own lesson.
A sector. Take two radii, O A and O B, and the arc between them. The part of the circle they close off is a sector. It's a slice of the circle, like a slice of pizza.

A sector can be a thin slice. It can be a quarter of the circle, when the central angle is ninety degrees. And a half, a semicircle, is a sector too. We'll learn the area of a sector in its own lesson.
And the last one, a segment. Take a chord, A B. The part of the circle between the chord and its arc is called a segment.
at: between the chord and its arc

slides.say: Don't mix it up with a sector. A sector is closed off by two radii and an arc. A segment is closed off by one chord and an arc. This small segment leaves the center O outside it. But a big segment, more than half the circle, can have O inside it. On the exam a segment usually appears as a shaded region between a chord and an arc.

Let's put it all together on one circle. Try to name each line before I do. Look at O A first. [short pause] O A goes from the center to the circle, so it's a radius. Now look at B C. [short pause] B C goes through the center, so it's a diameter. And it's also a chord, the longest one.
at: O A goes from the center
B C goes through the center

slides.say: Now look at D E. [short pause] D E joins two points on the circle, but it doesn't go through the center, so it's just a chord. And now the line at T. [short pause] It touches the circle at one point only, so it's a tangent.
at: And now the line at T

slides: That's it for the words we use in a circle. In the next lesson we start on the rules, the angles in a circle, and what we know about them. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
